web_evidence.note: The publisher's authorized excerpt presents Chapter One as sustained first-person narration in 1995, then begins Chapter Two in sustained third-person narration focused on Vianne in 1939.

web_evidence.title: The Nightingale — Excerpt — Kristin Hannah

person_note: The novel sustains two base-narration persons: an elderly participating narrator tells the 1995 frame in first person, while the much longer World War II narrative is told externally in third person through Vianne and Isabelle. The authorized publisher excerpt directly displays the chapter-level switch, and a scholarly whole-book review confirms that first-person frame chapters intermittently interrupt the third-person wartime narrative through the end. The quote set independently contains repeated first-person frame passages and sustained third-person interior scenes. First-person dialogue, epigraphs, maxims, and figurative embedded uses were not promoted to separate narration. No credible contrary structural evidence remains.
